title: Vetala Story 19: The Thief Who Became King
summary: The Vetala said: 'O King! Listen to the tale of Shurapala the Outlaw!'...
keywords: vetala story 19: the thief who became king
full_text:
King Vikramaditya recaptured the corpse and carried it through the gale.

The Vetala said: 'O King! Listen to the tale of Shurapala the Outlaw!'

Shurapala was a notorious highway bandit who robbed rich merchants. When an army of foreign invaders attacked the defenseless city at night while the cowardly king fled, the bandit mobilized his five hundred outlaws, ambushed the invaders, and drove them from the kingdom, saving the citizens from massacre.

The citizens assembled and crowned the bandit as their sovereign.

The Vetala asked: 'King Vikramaditya, was it lawful for citizens to crown a convicted thief?'

Vikramaditya answered: 'It was entirely lawful. Kingship is defined not by birth or title, but by the willingness to protect the people with one's life. He who protects the innocent when the crowned king flees is the true sovereign appointed by dharma.'

'Justly said!' cried the Vetala, and flew back to his tree.
moral: Courage and civic protection elevate even a thief to the seat of a king.
